Commentary.Commentary: The umpires are on the field. The Australian players rush out on the field and take their respective positions. Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul are the opening batters for the West Indies. Mitchell Starc has the new pink ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
...THIRD INNINGS...

West Indies, on the other hand, were brilliant with the new ball, but will be a bit disappointed as they let the Aussies get way closer to the total than they would have wanted. Kemar Roach got the wicket of Steven Smith in the very first over to set the tone and Alzarri Joseph followed it up with another. Joseph was the best bowler with four wickets while Kemar Roach ended up with three. However, in the middle phase and towards the end, they gave away a lot of runs and let the hosts come back in the game. Shamar Joseph and Kevin Sinclair chipped in with one each as well. Now, it is up to their opening batters to see out the session under lights without much damage as it will be a tricky phase for them.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! That is the end of a brave innings by Nathan Lyon! Alzarri Joseph drops it short and over middle. Nathan Lyon, with the intent to hit, pulls at it wildly. He gets hurried on and ends up nicking the upper edge. Joshua Da Silva takes a sharp catch behind the stumps and the umpire raises a finger straight away. Both Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon walk off the field as they have declared their innings with a deficit of 22 runs hanging over their heads. A good strategy as the Aussies want to get a strong start with the new ball in hand, under the lights.

Commentary.Commentary: With that wicket of Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins has declared the innings! Australia still trails by 22 runs but they wanted to have a go at West Indies under lights and it will be an interesting half an hour or so till Stumps. Australia got off to a nightmare start, losing Steven Smith in the first over and Marnus Labuschagne followed suit. Usman Khawaja was stranded at one losing partners at the other as they were in a precarious position at 54/5. However, Alex Carey' counter-attacking fifty and his partnership of 96 runs with Khawaja got them back in the game. Carey did get out, but it was the skipper, Pat Cummins who led from the front with his highest individual score in Tests and helped the Aussies get near the total, and now they will look to make early inroads before the end of Day 2.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Kevin Sinclair gets his maiden Test wicket! The backflips are out at the Gabba. He also gets the big fish, Usman Khawaja, and finally breaks the partnership that the Windies desperately wanted. This is flighted, full and around off, turns away a shy bit, Usman Khawaja eyes light up and he goes for the big drive but only manages to get an outside edge towards first slip where Alick Athanaze takes a sharp catch. Sinclair brings out his cartwheel and backflip celebration and this is just the start for home in Test cricket. A fantastic knock from Khawaja finally comes to an end. SESSION SUMMARY - 137 runs and 3 wickets in 25.1 overs! Once again, we see a wicket fall in the last over before the end of a session. Australia started the session in a difficult position. Mitchell Marsh played a few attacking blows but Alzarri Joseph got the better of him. Just like the Windies, it was the sixth-wicket partnership for the Aussies that steadied things. Usman Khawaja held one end solidly while Alex Carey took on the attack and found the boundaries regularly. He got a reprieve early on when the ball hit the bails but it remained on the stumps and went on to register his fastest Test fifty and added 96 runs along with Khawaja. However, he fell victim to a short-ball plan as Shamar Joseph got his first wicket of the match while it was Joseph again who dismissed Mitchell Starc just before the end of the session. The onus will be now on Khawaja to manage along with the tail-enders to reduce the trail and get close to the Windies' total if not past that, but that looks a bit difficult. West Indies will look to quickly wrap things up under lights in the third session. Join as at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT) to see how things unfold in the third session.

We don't often see the mighty Australia in a tough spot while playing at the Gabba but today, the Windies have managed to do just that. Steven Smith, the new opening partner for Usman Khawaja couldn't take his innings deep as he was trapped in front of the stumps. Marnus Labuschagne, again unusual for him to play a rash shot and get caught out in the slip region. Cameron Green played a few good-looking shots but the field placement of Kraigg Brathwaite, near the short cover region, led to his dismissal. Travis Head went fetching for his very first ball angling down the leg side and managed to nick it. The keeper made no mistake behind the stumps and it led to his dismissal just before the session. Now, it is very important for Australia to put up a good partnership and manage to inch closer to the score West Indies has put up for them. Join us for the second session of Day 2 at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT).

The players head out to the dressing rooms for the dinner break. West Indies, before the break had managed to put a strong score on the board. The bowling duo of Alzarri Joseph and Kemar Roach have managed to wreak havoc on the Aussies in the second innings. Kemar Roach gave the first breakthrough after dismissing Steven Smith, trapping the veteran in front of the stumps. The troublesome, Marnus Labuschagne also had to depart off the bowling of Alzarri Joseph and courtesy of a brilliant catch by the debutant Kevin Sinclair. Then, Kemar Roach got two wickets in the last two deliveries before the break by dismissing Cameron Green and Travis Head. They have managed to put the Aussies on the back foot here in Gabba. Now, they will look for a few more wickets in the second session.

OUT! TAKEN! TWO IN TWO FOR ROACH! The crowd at Gabba goes silent now! An unlucky way to get dismissed for Travis Head, but West Indies won't mind one bit. Kemar Roach serves this one fuller as well, but angling down the leg side, Travis Head stays there and tries to flick it away but only manages to nick it behind where Joshua Da Silva moves quickly to his right to take a sharp catch. Head goes back for a golden duck and Australia are in all sorts of trouble now. THAT WILL BE DINNER ON DAY 2!

This one is fuller again and on off, jags back in sharply and skids thorough, Steven Smith takes a big step across to work it away, but misses it completely due to the movement and gets hit on the pads right on the front of the stumps. A huge appeal for LBW, but the umpire says no. West Indies takes the review. UltraEdge shows no bat involved and Ball Tracking indicates three reds. Early blow for Australia as Smith walks back!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Kemar Roach to Steven Smith, OUT! lbw b Kemar Roach.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh.. beautiful! Kemar Roach pitches this one up, on middle, Steven Smith stays in his crease and presents the full face of the bat to play a classy straight drive past the bowler for a boundary.
